parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, border/facility rule, police targeting or custody exposure is documented, and no universal-exposure measure is shown. Against that, same-sex conduct is criminalised, there is no anti-discrimination recourse, registration of LGBT groups is refused despite constitutional rights recognised, official/religious hostility and significant stigma are documented, and advocacy evidence says people stay closeted for fear of rejection. Pride was police-escorted and 2021 guidelines name gender-identity violence, but these do not create operative visitor protection. Outing therefore risks criminal-law leverage, discrimination and violence with thin remedy, without documented state sweeps or imprisonment for presentation.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; foreign passport read as issued. No documented entry rule, marker rejection or border treatment for mismatched documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch, if noticed, could interact with criminalised same-sex law, but no such use is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention, birth-sex custody or verification exam for trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom, ward, shelter or other facility exclusion for trans visitors.

care_services.exposure: 2019 LGBTQ-wide survey: 59% disrespect/discrimination and 30% denied care at public facilities; dated and not trans-specific, so limited current weight. Access risk noted.
care_services.protection: 2013 health policy requires family-planning services regardless of sexual orientation; 2012 HIV campaign included same-sex couples.
care_services.interaction: Policy protections sit beneath unchanged criminal law and no discrimination statute.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex relations criminalised for men and women; trans visitor in locally classed same-sex relationship falls under it. No documented police lever used against gender-nonconforming people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2021 guidelines include freedom from discrimination by sexual orientation and define gender-based violence by gender identity, naming LGBT people higher-risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Criminal law is secondary for solo trans visitor but becomes primary if travelling with same-sex partner.

minors_guardians.exposure: No visitor-specific minor exposure documented. Resident same-sex adoption ban does not apply to visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two individual 2015 murders of lesbian/gay people in one town; no trans-specific rate, no later case documented. Significant societal stigma and fear of rejection documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2018 Pride of 2,000+ was police-escorted; welcoming LGBTIQ church reopened 2018.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Visibility coexists with stigma; no documented pattern of police protection or failure for trans victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No broad anti-discrimination protections; LGBT registration refused 2019, upheld 2022 though court accepted privacy/expression rights; 2023 supreme court reportedly voided refusal but ministry still refuses. No national advocacy body.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional rights accepted in court reasoning; no demonstrated visitor remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper rights without registration or discrimination law leave thin practical recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity than 0.35-B: no documented routine police stops, confiscations, extortion or nuisance fines for trans visitors, whereas 0.35-B centres on that state practice.

Similar tier: no credible imprisonment/execution for presentation, but durable exposure and weak remedies. Here exposure is via criminalised same-sex law and stigma rather than universal registration.
Lower/safer? No: 0.55-B has administrative denial with appeal desk and consular process; here criminalisation plus no anti-discrimination recourse and official hostility make remedy weaker.
Materially below 0.65-A: no national equality protection, no documented apology/compensation remedy, and documented stigma/closeting, unlike brief detention followed by working accountability.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no documented tier-1 universal exposure or organised targeting, so not in 0.25-0.35 range. But criminalised same-sex conduct, no discrimination law, blocked registration, official hostility and significant stigma place it at tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse. Positive signals—police-escorted Pride, inclusive guidelines, court recognition of privacy/expression—are real but dated, policy-level or resident-facing and do not operate as visitor protection. Border, facilities, custody and minors are largely undocumented, not safe. Net: elevated risk, around 0.44.
